## Job Description
**The Role**
Canopius is looking for an experienced Workday Financials Reporting Analyst to design, build, and maintain custom reporting and analytics across the Workday Financials domain. The successful candidate will translate finance and accounting requirements into robust custom reports, with a particular emphasis on Composite, Matrix, and Advanced reports used to deliver financial statements such as income statements, plan-versus-actuals comparisons, and other consolidated management reporting
This is a 9 month Day Rate Contract inside IR35.
This is a hands-on build role. You will own report definitions end to end: selecting the right data source, constructing the necessary sub-reports, assembling them into Composite reports, applying calculations and formatting, and validating output against finance sign-off criteria. You will work closely with finance stakeholders, accounting teams, and the wider Workday configuration team, and you are expected to review your own work rigorously before it goes to a business owner. ## **Responsibilities**
* Gather and refine reporting requirements from finance and accounting stakeholders, and translate them into report designs that are accurate, performant, and maintainable.
* Design and build custom reports across relevant Workday report types, including Advanced and Matrix, selecting the appropriate type for each requirement.
* Design, build, and maintain Composite reports that combine data from multiple sub-reports into a single consolidated output, including:
1. Building the underlying Advanced and Matrix sub-reports and enabling the correct business objects for filtering and grouping so that each sub-report references all enabled objects.
2. Configuring control field columns, data columns, lookup field value columns, calculation columns, and empty columns.
3. Applying repeating column groups (for example repeating by company or cost Centre), prompt sets, analytic indicators, conditional formatting overrides, and drill-to report links.
4. Using dynamic control fields for accounting work tags so that a single Composite report can generate multiple financial report variants.
* Build Matrix reports that summarise and drill down on data, configuring row and column groupings, summarisation, and field values groups, both as standalone outputs and as sub-reports for Composite reporting.
* Build Advanced reports, including the use of dynamic data rows, sub-filters, and sort orders, both as standalone outputs and as sub-reports for Composite reporting.
* Build and reuse calculated fields to reshape, format, retrieve, and derive data not directly available on the report data source.
* Select appropriate report data sources, distinguishing between standard, indexed and Prism data sources, and tune reports for performance (indexed fields for filtering, faceting, aggregation, and grouping).
* Validate and troubleshoot reports using tools such as Validate Composite Report, Report Definition Usages, and the Clean Up Custom Report task; resolve join exceptions, anomalies, and warnings.
* Configure output, sharing, scheduling, and report groups (including bursting) so that finance deliverables such as year-end statements run reliably and on time.
* Manage report security appropriately, working within the relevant security domains and ensuring users see only the data they are entitled to.
* Document report designs clearly and prepare design specifications for review and business sign-off.
* Support testing, reconciliation of report output to source data, and knowledge transfer to finance users.
## **Skills**
* Extensive, demonstrable experience building and maintaining Workday Composite, Matrix, and Advanced reports. This is the core requirement for the role: + Composite: fluency with sub-reports, control field and data columns, the full range of row types, calculation expressions, outline structures, repeating column groups, prompt sets, analytic indicators, and drill-to links, and the ability to explain the design trade-offs behind each.
+ Matrix: confident configuration of row and column groupings, summarisation, drill-down, and field values groups, and use of Matrix reports as Composite sub-reports.
+ Advanced: confident use of filters, sub-filters, dynamic data rows, sort orders, and use of Advanced reports as Composite sub-reports.
* Proven track record building custom reports across the broader Workday report catalogue (Trending and others) in a Workday Financials context.
* Strong understanding of Workday reporting fundamentals: business objects, report data sources, and fields, and how data source selection drives both available fields and report performance.
* Experience authoring calculated fields and applying them within reports.
* Solid grasp of financial reporting concepts, including income statements, plan versus actuals, variance analysis, and drill-down by dimensions such as ledger account, cost centre, and region.
* Rigorous, detail-oriented approach: you reconcile output to source, surface edge cases early, and review your own work before it is distributed.
* Clear written communication for design documentation and stakeholder sign-off.
* Exposure to Workday Accounting Center and/or Prism Analytics, and an understanding of how upstream data flows into Financials reporting.
* Experience with dynamic control fields for accounting work tags and configuring a single Composite report to produce multiple statement variants.
* Report performance tuning on high-volume tenants (indexed data sources, optimisation for performance).
* Insurance industry experience is highly desirable, with the Lloyd's of London market preferable. Experience in another regulated financial-services environment will also be considered.
* Configuration of dashboards and worklets and enabling reports as web services for downstream integration.

## Build the systems that automate parts procurement
## About Carpata
Carpata is building the infrastructure to automate parts procurement across the automotive aftersales industry, a market worth more than $2 trillion globally. The hard part is fitment. Garages, dealers and fleets spend a lot of time working out which part fits which vehicle, and they still order the wrong one too often. Solve that and the rest of the process can be automated. Give us a registration and a job, and we return the right parts and let you order them from your supplier.
We are a seed-stage company with paying customers in production. The founders have built and sold automotive technology businesses before. We are backed by Concept Ventures, Nosara Capital and angels from CarWow, JustPark, Autotrader and Bumper.
## The Role
Your first project is to automate the vehicle data pipeline that keeps our catalogue current. Every vehicle on the UK road has to be matched to the right entry in the catalogue, the source data changes every month, and parts of that process still need an engineer to run them. You will build the pipeline that does it on a schedule, so that our catalogue team reviews what it proposes rather than operating it. The work is a mix of data engineering, matching records across sources that describe the same vehicle differently, and production engineering on AWS. It is not infrastructure-heavy: the Lambda, Postgres and Terraform foundations are already in place.
Beyond that, the work follows the roadmap. We are building in three areas: catalogue intelligence, which is identifying the right part for a given vehicle and catching errors before customers do; workflow automation, which covers search, ordering and integrations with the systems garages and dealers already use; and supply, connecting more suppliers so customers can order through us whoever they buy from. Over three months you would work in at least two of these. We are a small team and do not specialise early, so we need someone comfortable moving between backend, data and, when needed, front-end work.
You would get up to speed with our Lead Engineer, who owns the platform architecture, and work day to day with Pete, our CTO, and with our catalogue lead, who brings the automotive knowledge.
### The Stack
TypeScript throughout the platform, with some existing data tooling in Python. Postgres. AWS Lambda with Terraform. A GraphQL API. Next.js and React on the front end. Most of our code is written with Claude Code, so engineers spend more of their time on design, on directing the implementation, and on reviewing and testing what comes back. We are still working out the best way to build like this, and we want people who are interested in that question, not just tolerant of the tools. The language you have written most in matters less than it used to, though TypeScript is home.
## Why Join Now
Most of the hard problems are still open, and there are not many of us to solve them. Whoever joins now will have a large say in what we build and how we build it, including how we work with AI tools.
## Who We Are Looking For
A software engineer, backend or full stack, who will take on a hard problem and see it through, rather than work through tickets.
* You have turned a process that ran by hand into one that runs without a person in the loop.
* You ship small and often: pull requests merged the week they open, then improved on what breaks.
* You build with AI tools every day, check what they produce, and know where they fall short.
* You back your decisions with numbers and share them when they are bad as well as when they are good.
* You have worked somewhere small, where you had to work out the approach rather than be handed a specification.
* You go for the hardest part of the problem first, not the predictable route.
* You build for a mechanic at 6pm on a Friday, not for a demo.
Experience on data projects helps but is not essential. An interest in cars helps but is not essential either.
## This Role Is Not For You If
* You need the problem fully defined before you start.
* You would rather perfect something than ship it.
* You think "good enough" is acceptable when the customer needs it right.
* You design for the happy path and hope.
* You dismiss feedback that challenges an assumption rather than getting interested in why.
## Role Details
#### Length
Three months to start, five days a week. If it is working for both sides we would look to extend, or talk about a permanent role. Equity is offered to full-time employees.
#### Rate
We talk about the day rate on the first call.
#### Working Pattern
Hybrid. Three days a week in our office at Elephant & Castle, two remote.
#### Start
As soon as you are available.
#### Visa
We cannot sponsor visas.
### Hiring Process
1. 45 minutes with Pete, our CTO: your background, the work you are proudest of, and what we are building.
2. 60 minutes technical, in person, with one of our engineers.
3. 60 minutes with Matt, our CEO.
We give clear feedback at each step and aim to come back within a week.
## How To Apply
Email your CV and a short note to info@carpata.com.
If you do not tick every box but the problem interests you, get in touch anyway.

* **Quote-to-cash** — HubSpot through invoicing, deferred revenue, and collections, with ARR a live, reconciled number; plus the gatekeeper that protects what enters the ledger.
* **Reporting and the raise** — a clean actuals layer that feeds board reporting with no manual prep, plus the diligence-ready numbers behind the next fundraise.

* Hands-on ownership of month-end close, management accounts, and balance-sheet reconciliations. Non-negotiable — you'll own numbers people rely on from your first month.

* **Agent-first automation** — you build, not just use. Fluent from no-code (n8n, Zapier) to MCP and code when a workflow outgrows it; you automate first and hire second.
* Baseline payroll and UK compliance awareness — enough to spot when a number is wrong.
* Comfortable in startup pace and ambiguity, and happy to own the cross-functional problem when it needs an owner.
**Nice to have:** SaaS revenue recognition (IFRS 15 / ASC 606); equity accounting (IFRS 2); HubSpot–ERP integration; SQL/Python; multi-entity consolidation and FX.

In 12 months: books closed in days not weeks, with most journals and reconciliations running without you. A live daily cash position across the UK and US, forecast-driven. Inspiring people and communities to age and live well in later life Age UK Cornwall & The Isles of Scilly is seeking an exceptional Chief Executive to lead one of Cornwall’s most respected charities into its next chapter.

Our next Chief Executive will inherit a financially stable organisation with an excellent reputation, committed colleagues and volunteers, strong governance and significant reach across Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

You will work with our Board, colleagues, volunteers and partners to develop our strategy, strengthen and diversify our income, continue to evolve our services and increase our influence across the wider health and care system.
You will also build strong relationships across the Age UK network, ensuring that Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly contributes to and benefits from national learning, policy, collaboration and opportunities.
**The leader we are seeking**
We are looking for a leader who combines strategic vision with the credibility to guide a complex, servicedelivery organisation. You will empower people to thrive, build leadership capacity and unite colleagues, volunteers and partners behind a shared purpose. You will be comfortable operating beyond organisational boundaries and developing influential relationships across health and social care, local government, commissioners, funders, businesses, communities and the wider voluntary sector.
Commercial awareness and financial acumen will be essential. You will understand what it takes to lead a sustainable organisation, diversify income and demonstrate the impact and value of our work. ***An exciting opportunity has become available for a Highly Specialist Speech and Language Therapist to join our team at Woodrowe House.***
***Woodrowe House is a leading neurological complex care service located in the picturesque outskirts of Leicester, in Markfield. We specialise in complex care and treatment for individuals with acquired brain injuries (ABI) and other neurological conditions, including stroke and spinal injuries. Our mission is to provide a supportive and expert environment for long-term and short-term care needs.***
**Job Purpose**
As an integral member of the multidisciplinary team (MDT), you will manage a specialist caseload of individuals with complex neurological needs, assessing and supporting their Speech, Communication and Language Needs (SCLN) and Eating, Drinking and Swallowing (EDS) needs. Acting as the lead for Speech and Language Therapy within the service, you will deliver evidence-based assessment and intervention in line with the Cygnet SLT Pathway for Neurological Complex Care, supporting rehabilitation, risk management, safety, wellbeing and quality of life.
You will work with patients across our three care pathways at Woodrowe House:
* Slow Stream Rehabilitation: Goal-focused, therapeutically-led placements for people who have stepped down from acute rehabilitation settings.
* Long-term & Maintenance: Packages designed for individuals with progressive or highly dependent needs to prevent deterioration and improve quality of life.
* Short-term Placements: Providing respite care allowing the caregiver to take a much-needed break from their duties, whilst knowing that their loved one is safe and well-supported.
The role will contribute to the delivery of person-centred care, provide specialist advice and consultation, support staff training and competency development, and lead the implementation of interventions and environmental approaches that optimise communication, swallowing function, participation, independence and quality of life for individuals with complex neurological and rehabilitation needs.

## Description
**Join us at EIT:**
At the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT), we're on a mission to translate scientific discovery into real world impact. We bring together visionary scientists, technologists, engineers, researchers, educators and innovators to tackle humanity's greatest challenges in four transformative areas:
* Health, Medical Science & Generative Biology
* Food Security & Sustainable Agriculture
* Climate Change & Managing CO[2]
* Artificial Intelligence & Robotics
This is ambitious work - work that demands curiosity, courage, and a relentless drive to make a difference. At EIT, you'll join a community built on excellence, innovation, tenacity, trust, and collaboration, where bold ideas become real-world breakthroughs. Together, we push boundaries, embrace complexity, and create solutions to scale ideas from lab to society. Explore more at .
**Welcome to the Plant Biology Institute:**
The Plant Biology Institute, headed by Professor Steve Kelly, is a key part of the Ellison Institute of Technology (EIT) Oxford. The institute aims to develop impactful and commercially sustainable solutions for improving global food production and planetary health through pioneering plant science research.
The Plant Biology Institute will unite world-class researchers who are focused on expanding the frontiers of plant science. Our research is focused on enhancing our ability to feed the planet while simultaneously improving the climate and ecosystem outcomes of food production. By embedding cutting-edge plant science research within an organisation that is focused on solving global challenges at scale, we aim to accelerate the timeline from discovery to global impact.
Areas of exploration include:
* Improved plant productivity, both indoors and outside.
* Reduced reliance on inputs including water, fertilisers, pesticides, and herbicides.
* Novel decarbonised plant-based production platforms for food and medicines.
* Advanced technologies that speed up discovery and deployment in plants.
Researchers will have access to state-of-the-art laboratory and plant growth facilities and have opportunities to collaborate with experts at the forefront of research on AI, automation, and generative biology across the EIT ecosystem. They will also work with global leaders in market development, commercialisation, and impact creation. The Plant Biology Institute has long-term substantial funding to support the unique scale and ambition of its vision.
**Your Role:**
EIT is seeking an experienced **Vector Design Manager** to join the Crop Transformation Pipeline team within the Plant Biology Institute. This role will lead the design, build strategy, quality control and release of transformation vectors and genome editing reagents for gene edited and transgenic crop programme.
The successful candidate will be a technical authority in commercial vector design, plant molecular biology and crop genome editing technologies. They will translate trait and editing objectives into transformation-ready vector designs, ensuring that constructs are fit-for-purpose for high-throughput transformation, event recovery, molecular characterisation and downstream product development.
This role is critical to building an industrial-grade vector design capability for crops including corn, wheat and other strategic species. The candidate will establish design standards, construct QC criteria, vendor workflows, sequence/data management processes and clear handover packages for transformation and event delivery teams.
The candidate will own the upstream design-to-vector-release process, ensuring that all constructs entering transformation are technically sound, traceable, QC-approved and aligned with commercial and regulatory expectations.
**Your Responsibilities:**
* Lead vector design strategy for gene edited and transgenic crop projects, including expression cassette architecture, promoter and terminator selection, selectable/reporter marker choice, cargo design, guide RNA modules, donor templates and multiplex editing configurations.
* Translate trait biology, editing objectives and transformation requirements into vectors suitable for Agrobacterium-mediated, biolistic and emerging plant delivery systems.
* Provide expert guidance on CRISPR/Cas systems, Cas12, base editing, prime editing, multiplex editing, homology-directed repair, transgene-free approaches and marker-free design options where appropriate.
* Develop commercial-grade design rules that consider transformation performance, event quality, freedom-to-operate, stewardship, regulatory needs, trait stacking, construct stability and downstream assay ability.
* Own construct intake, design review, annotation, nomenclature, barcode strategy, version control, sequence verification, risk assessment and release criteria before vectors enter transformation workflows.
* Manage internal and external vector build activities, including DNA synthesis, cloning, plasmid QC, sequence confirmation, Agrobacterium strain selection, Agrobacterium introduction, glycerol stock tracking and vector delivery to transformation teams.
* Work closely with event delivery and genotyping colleagues to ensure vectors are designed with the right molecular assay strategy, including junction assays, copy number assays, guide/edit assays and marker/backbone detection.
* Build and maintain a structured vector inventory and construct database using ELN, LIMS and sequence management tools, ensuring full traceability from request through vector release.
* Create SOPs, design templates, QC checklists, construct handover forms and decision records to support reproducible, auditable and scalable vector delivery.
* Track vector design and build milestones, budgets, vendor dependencies, quality risks and delivery timelines, escalating blockers early and proposing contingency plans.
* Partner with legal, IP, regulatory, procurement and external collaborators to ensure vector designs and material transfers are aligned with programme and commercial requirements.
* Train and mentor scientists, research associates and project teams in vector design principles, sequence review, construct documentation and transformation-readiness criteria.
* The successful candidate will combine deep molecular design expertise with strong operational discipline. They will help reduce failed transformation cycles by ensuring that constructs are technically robust, well documented and suitable for downstream event confirmation before experiments begin.
The candidate will be expected to identify opportunities for IP creation, support commercial vector design decisions and contribute to EIT's mission of translating plant science into high-impact, scalable crop improvement technologies.
## Requirements
**Essential Skills, Qualifications & Experience:**
* PhD in Plant Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, Genetics, Genomics, Crop Science or a related discipline, or MSc with significant relevant industry experience. At least 5-7 years of experience in plant biotechnology, molecular design, genome editing or vector development.
* Demonstrated expertise in plant vector design for crop transformation, including binary vectors, expression cassette design, regulatory elements, selectable/reporter systems, multi-gene constructs and transformation-compatible plasmid architecture.
* Strong understanding of genome editing technologies, including CRISPR/Cas systems, guide RNA design, multiplex editing, base editing, prime editing, donor template design and edited event confirmation requirements.
* Experience with construct design and sequence analysis tools such as Benchling, SnapGene, Geneious, Vector NTI or equivalent platforms, with strong capability in sequence annotation, alignment and design review.
* Practical understanding of crop transformation workflows

We’re currently on an exciting journey as we drive forward significant organisational, people, process, and AI and technology transformation to become a more forward-thinking, proactive regulator. We will use data more effectively to drive better regulatory decisions and build greater cohesion across our broad financial services remit.
Significant improvements in digital enablement, business intelligence, market data and information management maturity are all being pursued to maintain our position as a world leader in financial services regulation. In March 2025, the FCA launched a new 5-year strategy to deepen trust, rebalance risk, support growth and improve lives. The FCA will focus on four priorities:
* Be a smarter regulator; predictable, purposeful and proportionate. The FCA will improve its processes and embrace technology to become more efficient and effective.
* Support sustained economic growth, by enabling investment, innovation and ensuring the continued competitiveness of the UK’s world-leading financial services.
* Help consumers navigate their financial lives by working with industry to boost trust, product innovation and ensuring the right information and support is available for people to take financial decisions.
* Fight financial crime, focusing on those who seek to use the fact they are regulated to do harm. It will go further to disrupt criminals and support firms to be an effective line of defence.
**The Role** We have an exciting opportunity for a permanent Head of AI & Technology Security Operations. This role is designed for an experienced manager, senior technical specialist, or existing Head of Department with proven experience of leading teams and operating at scale in a rapidly evolving digital and AI-driven operating environment. The successful candidate will strengthen their strategic and operational leadership while overseeing high-tempo, service-critical digital and AI operations.
The Head of AI & Technology Security Operations is accountable for ensuring that the FCA’s technology estate — including rapidly expanding AI capabilities — is robust, secure, and able to withstand, detect, and recover from disruption, failure, or exploitation.
The role brings together operational resilience, infrastructure governance, supplier oversight, and enterprise technology and AI-specific vulnerability management, ensuring that both traditional infrastructure and AI-enabled systems are designed, operated, and governed to remain safe, dependable, and trustworthy under stress. Working in close collaboration with C&IR (Cyber and Information Resilience), this HoD plays a critical leadership role in implementing and managing the technology controls needed to anticipate and mitigate AI-driven risks, including model vulnerabilities, upstream dependency risks, data poisoning, adversarial attacks, and control failures arising from increased autonomy and scale.

This is a fantastic development opportunity which will help to build expertise, experience and career skills in a senior, challenging and highly visible role.
The role will be reporting to the Chief Information Officer, and sit in the wider Data, Technology, and Innovation Division.

You will lead a skilled multidisciplinary department, working across high-impact digital and AI initiatives to strengthen technology and AI risk management, improve resilience and enable the safe adoption of emerging technologies. Collaborating closely with Cyber & Information Resilience, DTI leadership, product teams and front-line divisions, you will play a key role in driving meaningful change and reinforcing the FCA’s reputation as a trusted, innovative regulator.

* Leading the development and operation of the FCA’s AI vulnerability and threat management capability, identifying and mitigating risks linked to AI model weaknesses, adversarial threats, automation and agentic AI systems.

* Overseeing critical third-party and AI supply chain dependencies, including cloud platforms, AI model providers, managed services and data sources.
* Ensuring supplier, concentration and substitution risks are understood, monitored and managed effectively.
* Owning technology continuity strategies across data, digital and AI services, ensuring critical services can withstand disruption, degrade safely and recover effectively.
* Overseeing scenario testing, failover design, recovery validation and core service operations, including incident, problem and change management.
* Leading and developing multidisciplinary teams across technology risk, AI operations, supplier management, continuity and live service operations.
* Building strong capability, clear accountability and a culture where secure, resilient and dependable systems are a shared responsibility.
* Representing the FCA externally with government, regulators, industry bodies and standards organisations on technology, AI and operational resilience.
* Managing team budget, headcount, resources and IT supplier spend of approximately £80m.
* Championing innovation, continuous improvement and the safe adoption of emerging technologies to strengthen resilience, efficiency and value for money.

# Founding Principal Engineer

### **The Role**
We’re looking for a **Founding Principal Engineer** to join as a senior technical co-builder. This is not a purely hands-on-keyboard role, and it’s not a purely strategic one either. You’ll be the person who sets the technical direction, makes the hard architectural calls, and then ships the code alongside the founding team.
You’ll own the full stack — a React/TypeScript frontend, a Node.js/Express backend, a PostgreSQL data layer (Neon serverless via Drizzle ORM), and a growing set of AI-powered features. You’ll work directly with the founder on product decisions, help hire and shape the early engineering team, and establish the practices that the company will build on for years.
If you want to be the person who decides what “good engineering” looks like at a company before it has 100 engineers, this is that role.
### **What You’ll Do**
* **Own the architecture.** Make and document the decisions that define how the system scales — data model evolution, API design, real-time infrastructure (WebSockets), multi-tenant isolation, and authentication/RBAC.
* **Ship product.** Write production code across the stack: React 18/TypeScript on the frontend, Express/TypeScript on the backend, and SQL via Drizzle ORM. This is a senior IC role — you will build, not just review.
* **Drive AI integration.** Lead the design and implementation of AI-powered features using the Anthropic SDK — from generation and summarisation to agentic planning workflows.
* **Establish engineering standards.** Define the patterns, tooling, and review bar that new engineers will onboard into. Set up observability, testing strategy, CI/CD, and deployment discipline.
* **Collaborate on product.** Work closely with the founder to translate product requirements into technical solutions, push back when scope threatens quality, and propose better paths when you see them.
* **Grow the team.** Help recruit early engineers, conduct technical interviews, and mentor junior hires once the team expands.
* **Own the deployment story.** Manage Render deployments, the Neon PostgreSQL stack, AWS SES integration, and infrastructure decisions as the product scales.
### **What We’re Looking For**
*Required*
* 8+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 3 years in a senior or staff-level IC role.
* Strong full-stack TypeScript — you’re comfortable owning both React and Node.js/Express in the same week.
* Deep experience with relational databases and ORM layers (experience with Drizzle, Prisma, or similar is a plus; PostgreSQL fluency is essential).
* A track record of making architectural decisions under uncertainty and living with the consequences — you’ve seen what happens when you get these right and when you get them wrong.
* Experience building multi-tenant SaaS products — you understand the data isolation, performance, and security challenges that come with it.
* Strong product sensibility — you can tell the difference between a feature that solves a real problem and one that adds complexity for its own sake.
* Experience with LLM/AI feature development (Anthropic SDK, OpenAI, or similar).
* Familiarity with real-time patterns (WebSockets, SSE, optimistic UI).
* Experience with RBAC systems and permission modelling.
* Background in project management, resource planning, or financial tooling domains.
* Prior founding or early-stage startup experience.
### ***Nice to Have***
* Experience with LLM/AI feature development (Anthropic SDK, OpenAI, or similar).
* Familiarity with real-time patterns (WebSockets, SSE, optimistic UI).
* Experience with RBAC systems and permission modelling.
* Background in project management, resource planning, or financial tooling domains.
* Prior founding or early-stage startup experience.
### **Why Join Us?**
**You’ll shape the product, not just build it.** At this stage, engineering and product decisions are inseparable. Your technical choices will directly define what Forest.tools can and can’t do for customers.
**You’ll set the culture.** The first few engineers at any company establish the norms everyone else inherits. You’ll decide what good looks like — in code review, in system design, in how the team communicates.
**The stack is modern and intentional.** React 18, TypeScript end-to-end, Vite, TanStack Query, Drizzle ORM, Neon serverless Postgres, Anthropic SDK. No legacy baggage — just well-chosen tools and the freedom to keep improving them.
**The problem space is rich.** Project management, capacity planning, budget management, and strategic planning all in one platform. There are deep engineering challenges in data modelling, real-time state, multi-tenancy, and AI-assisted planning — and you’ll get to work on all of them.
**You’ll work with, not for.** This is a founding-team relationship. You’ll have a direct line to product decisions, customer conversations, and company direction from day one.

**An overview of this role**
Site Reliability Engineers keep GitLab's user-facing services and production systems running reliably at scale. They combine software engineering with operational excellence, applying sound engineering principles, automation, and continuous improvement to build, operate, and evolve our production infrastructure.
This is a single application for Site Reliability Engineering opportunities across Infrastructure Platforms. Rather than asking you to choose the right team or level upfront, we evaluate your skills holistically and match you to the opportunity that best aligns with your experience and our hiring needs. We hire Site Reliability Engineers from Intermediate through Senior Staff across multiple Infrastructure Platforms teams.
We don't expect every candidate to have experience with every technology in our environment. We're looking for engineers with strong technical fundamentals, a growth mindset, and the ability to learn quickly. We'll support you in becoming successful with GitLab's tools, systems, and ways of working.
**Please note: This position is open to candidates based in the United Kingdom only. Candidates based in the United States or Canada can apply to this posting:** **Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — AMER (Intermediate to Senior Staff)**
**How our SRE hiring works**
Because this is a single application for SRE roles across Infrastructure Platforms, our process is built to evaluate you once and match you well, rather than interviewing separately for every team.
* **Recruiter Screen:** A conversation about your background, what you're looking for, and the level and teams that fit, so we can point your process in the right direction.
* **Core Technical:** The shared assessment every SRE candidate takes, regardless of eventual team. A low-stress, collaborative discussion covering system architecture and incident review.
* **Hiring Manager Interview:** A conversation about ownership, judgment, execution, collaboration, and growth, the non-technical signals that make an SRE effective at GitLab.
* **Peer Technical:** Team-specific depth, run by SREs from the team you're most likely to join, focused on the problems that team actually works on.
* **Skip-Level Interview:** A conversation with a senior leader on values alignment, and how you'll work across teams.
After your interviews, we consider your performance alongside our current hiring needs to confirm the level and team where you'll do your best work. Interview results are a major factor, and final placement also reflects our active hiring priorities at the time.
**We’ll calibrate your level throughout the interview process based on the scope and impact of your experience.**
* Intermediate: You independently deliver meaningful reliability improvements within a defined area.
* Senior: You own complex reliability work end to end and raise the effectiveness of your team.
* Staff: You shape reliability across multiple teams, solving systemic problems and creating approaches others can reuse.
* Senior Staff: You set technical direction across a broader Infrastructure area and influence reliability strategy at organizational scale.
**What you'll do**
* Keep user-facing services and production systems reliable, scalable, and efficient
* Build automation and tooling that reduces toil and replaces manual work with repeatable, infrastructure-as-code-driven workflows
* Operate and troubleshoot production systems on Kubernetes, including deployments, rollouts, and scaling
* Write and maintain infrastructure as code, and ship changes safely through CI/CD and GitOps
* Participate in on-call, triage alerts, follow and improve runbooks, and escalate appropriately
* Contribute to the observability stack, using metrics, logs, and SLOs to detect symptoms early rather than just outages
* Take part in incident response and post-incident reviews, turning learnings into changes in automation and process
* Document runbooks, architecture decisions, and reviews so your findings become repeatable practices
**What you'll bring**
* Experience keeping production systems reliable, combining an operations mindset with real software engineering practice
* Experience building net-new infrastructure tooling and automation, not just configuring existing tools. For example, Terraform modules, Kubernetes operators or controllers, or production automation and services written from scratch
* The ability to read, debug, and reason about code. Most of our teams work in Go; some work in Ruby. You can discuss a piece of code's behavior, performance, and failure modes
* Experience with infrastructure as code, and with Kubernetes and its ecosystem, at a depth appropriate to your level
* Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (GCP or AWS)
* Familiarity with observability practices, including metrics, logging, alerting, and SLOs or SLIs, and using data to inform operational decisions
* Comfort participating in on-call and incident response, with a structured approach to troubleshooting under pressure
* Strong written communication and the ability to operate as a manager-of-one in an async, distributed environment
* A track record of using automation, and increasingly AI, to reduce toil and improve how you and your team work
* Alignment with GitLab's values and a commitment to working in accordance with them
**About the team**
Infrastructure Platforms is responsible for the availability, reliability, performance, and scalability of GitLab’s user-facing services, most notably GitLab.com. The organization spans teams across Production Engineering, GitLab Dedicated, GitLab Delivery, and Developer Experience, covering everything from the production fleet and networking platform to observability, incident response, deployment infrastructure, tenant scale, and our single-tenant Dedicated offering. We are a globally distributed, remote-first organization that works asynchronously, favors automation over toil, and uses monitoring, metrics, and clear ownership to continuously improve the reliability of GitLab at scale. # Regulatory Affairs Executive
Solihull, England, United Kingdom
**OVERVIEW:**
Working across both established and emerging product categories, you'll keep up to date on changing regulations, provide expert guidance to cross-functional teams and help ensure our products meet global compliance requirements. Partnering with Product, Sustainability, Legal and Company Secretariat teams, you'll be at the heart of responsible innovation, supporting Gymshark's growth while helping us do business the right way.
**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING:**
**Responsible for:**
* Supporting global regulatory compliance across markets, ensuring products, packaging, labelling and claims meet legal and regulatory requirements.
* Interpreting and communicating regulatory requirements to stakeholders, providing practical business guidance and supporting understanding of evolving compliance expectations
* Reviewing product compliance, including labelling, sizing, product information and marketing claims.
* Advising on product development, sustainability initiatives and consumer-facing claims to ensure compliance and reduce risk
* Conducting regulatory research and horizon scanning to identify emerging legislative, sustainability and market trends.
* Monitoring regulatory developments and translating them into actionable business recommendations.
* Delivering training and guidance to improve organisational understanding of compliance requirements.
* Acting as a cross-functional business partner, supporting compliance investigations, customer complaints and continuous improvement activities.
* Assisting legal team on investigations, claims and regulatory audits as necessary
**Accountable for:**
* Identifying and managing regulatory and sustainability risks impacting products, categories and markets.
* Supporting the resolution of product compliance issues with internal and external stakeholders.
* Influencing product development processes to ensure compliance and market readiness.
* Assessing emerging regulatory and technical issues and recommending practical solutions aligned with business objectives.
* Deputising for senior team members when required and supporting strategic projects.
**WHAT YOU'LL NEED: Essential Criteria:**
**Qualifications and Experience**
* Experience in regulatory affairs, product compliance, sustainability, quality, responsible sourcing or a related field, ideally within retail, consumer products, textiles or apparel.
* Experience using compliance, sustainability, product stewardship or data management systems is advantageous.
* Experience may have been gained within regulatory affairs, sustainability, product stewardship, responsible sourcing, quality or related compliance functions.
* Able to work independently and apply sound judgement to complex issues.
* Degree or equivalent qualification in law, science, engineering, sustainability, textiles, environmental management or a related discipline.
**Technical Knowledge**
* Understanding of regulatory, sustainability and responsible sourcing requirements relevant to apparel, textiles and consumer products.
* Knowledge of marketing claims, product information and compliance principles.
* Understanding of complaint management and corrective action processes.
**Skills**
* Ability to interpret complex requirements and translate them into practical business actions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a risk-based mindset.
* Experience monitoring emerging regulations, standards and sustainability initiatives.
* Ability to review product information, labels and marketing claims for compliance.
* Effective stakeholder management and communication skills.
* Strong organisational skills, able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
* Confident in influencing decisions and driving compliance-focused outcomes.
* Proactive, resilient and commercially aware.
* Confident in use of AI tools
* Strong record keeping
**CLOSING DATE: Monday 21st September 2026**
**LOCATION:**
Please note this is a hybrid role and requires the successful candidate to attend at least 3 days a week in GSIQ, Solihull, UK.

Who We Are:
IMG is a leading global sports marketing agency, specializing in media rights management and sales, multi-channel content production and distribution, brand partnerships, strategic consulting, digital services, and event management. It powers growth of revenues, fanbases and IP for more than 250 federations, associations, events, and teams, including the National Football League, English Premier League, International Olympic Committee, National Hockey League, Major League Soccer, ATP and WTA Tours, the AELTC (Wimbledon), Euroleague Basketball, CONMEBOL, World Rugby, DP World Tour, and The R&A, as well as UFC, WWE, and PBR. TKO owns iconic properties including UFC, the world’s premier mixed martial arts organization; WWE, the global leader in sports entertainment; and PBR, the world’s premier bull riding organization. TKO also services and partners with major sports rights holders through IMG, an industry-leading global sports marketing agency; and On Location, a global leader in premium experiential hospitality.
Working Conditions
* Permanent Position, Mon-Fri, 9am-5pm
* This role is based at our facilities in Stockley Park, Uxbridge, with hybrid working options where applicable.
* You may be required to work unsociable hours, including occasional weekends or on-call rotations, to support live operations and critical systems.
* Occasional travel may be required depending on project and client needs.
IMG is looking for a Site Reliability Engineer to help design, build, operate, and continuously improve resilient, secure, and highly available platforms that underpin our digital, cloud, and broadcast-adjacent services. This role is suited to someone who combines strong infrastructure and software engineering capability with an operational mindset, and who can help embed reliability engineering practices across systems that support live, business-critical environments.
The successful candidate will play a key role in improving service reliability, observability, incident response, automation, and disaster recovery readiness across IMG platforms, while working closely with engineering, operations, and project stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities and Accountabilities
* Design, build, and maintain reliable, scalable infrastructure and platform services across on-premises and cloud environments.
* Improve service availability, latency, performance, and operational efficiency through engineering-led reliability practices.
* Build and enhance observability across services and infrastructure, including monitoring, logging, alerting, dashboards, and service health indicators.
* Define and maintain SLIs, SLOs, alerting standards, and operational runbooks for critical services.
* Automate infrastructure provisioning, configuration, deployment, and recovery processes using Infrastructure as Code and scripting.
* Partner with software, platform, broadcast engineering, and operational teams to improve release quality, resilience, and supportability.
* Act as an escalation point for production incidents, leading or supporting rapid diagnosis, mitigation, communication, and post-incident follow-up.
* Drive root cause analysis and corrective actions following incidents, with a focus on prevention and continuous improvement.
* Support the design, testing, and documentation of high availability, backup, failover, and disaster recovery arrangements.
* Help enforce security, access control, patching, and operational best practices across infrastructure and services.
* Optimise system capacity, cost, and performance across environments.
* Produce and maintain clear technical documentation, operational procedures, and support handover materials.
* Support live event and critical operational workflows where reliability, rapid response, and stakeholder communication are essential.
* Contribute to technical planning for new services, migrations, and platform enhancements, ensuring resilience is designed in from the start.
* Improve reliability, stability, and recoverability of IMG’s platform services.
* Reduced mean time to detect and resolve incidents through better observability and response processes.
* Higher levels of automation across provisioning, deployment, remediation, and operational support.
* Clearer operational ownership, documentation, and service standards across critical environments.
* Stronger resilience for live and client-facing workflows through tested failover and recovery approaches.
Knowledge and Experience
Mandatory
* Proven experience in a Site Reliability Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Platform Engineer, or similar role.
* Strong knowledge of Linux and operating system fundamentals.
* Strong hands-on experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
* Experience with containerisation and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
* Strong experience with CI/CD tooling and modern software delivery practices.
* Hands-on experience with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or CloudFormation.
* Experience with monitoring, logging, and alerting tooling, and with designing actionable observability solutions.
* Solid understanding of networking, security, system architecture, and distributed systems principles.
* Strong scripting or programming capability in Python, Bash, or similar languages.
* Experience working in high-availability, live production, or other business-critical operational environments.
* Strong troubleshooting skills, calm decision-making under pressure, and a continuous improvement mindset.

We are a Registered Organisation of the Chartered Institute for Archaeologists. More importantly, though we study the past, we are a forward-looking and innovative business, keen to help our clients stay ahead of the game.
## The Role
We are looking to appoint an experienced **Built Heritage specialist at Principal level** to lead and develop Headland Archaeology’s Historic Building Recording and buildings archaeology capability.
This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced buildings archaeologist, architectural historian or built heritage professional to take technical leadership of a growing area of our consultancy work and contribute to some of the UK’s most significant heritage and infrastructure projects.
The successful candidate will lead the investigation, recording, analysis and interpretation of historic buildings and places, working from initial research and project design through field investigation, assessment, analysis, reporting and publication.
You will work closely with colleagues across Headland’s Consultancy team and the wider RSK Group, alongside archaeologists, built heritage specialists, landscape specialists and other environmental disciplines. You will also engage directly with clients, Conservation Officers, statutory consultees, academics and other specialist contributors.
As a Principal-level appointment, you will provide technical leadership and quality assurance, manage complex projects and programmes of work, mentor and develop junior colleagues and help shape the future development of Headland’s Historic Building Recording service.
An important part of the role will be supporting the development of our graduate and early-career Built Heritage staff, sharing your expertise and helping build a strong and sustainable buildings archaeology specialism within the wider team.
**Key responsibilities**
You will lead and contribute to a varied portfolio of Historic Building Recording and Built Heritage projects. Responsibilities will include:
* Leading historic Building Recording and buildings archaeology projects from initial scoping and project design through investigation, analysis, reporting, publication and archive.
* Investigating and interpreting historic buildings through the integration of physical fabric, documentary and archival research, and wider archaeological and historical evidence.
* Designing appropriate programmes of building recording, research and analysis, and preparing and reviewing Written Schemes of Investigation, Project Designs, research frameworks and scopes of work.
* Producing and technically reviewing high-quality Historic Building Recording reports and other Built Heritage outputs, including contributions to professional and academic publication.
* Providing specialist Historic Building Recording advice to wider heritage projects, including built heritage and setting assessments, major infrastructure projects and interdisciplinary programmes of archaeological and landscape research.
* Leading and coordinating project teams and specialist contributors, including external specialists, academics and subcontractors where required.
* Building effective relationships with clients, Conservation Officers, statutory consultees and other heritage stakeholders, providing clear and proportionate technical advice.
* Preparing and reviewing fee proposals, scopes and budgets, and managing projects to agreed technical, programme and commercial requirements.
* Providing technical leadership for Historic Building Recording within Headland, including developing standards, methodologies and guidance and identifying opportunities for innovation and service development.
* Mentoring, training and providing technical direction to graduate, junior and other colleagues, helping to build Headland's Historic Building Recording capability.
The successful candidate will initially have the opportunity to contribute to a significant programme of analysis and publication relating to historic buildings and places, with themes including agricultural architecture, wartime buildings and monuments, entertainment and leisure landscapes, railway heritage, medieval and post-medieval landscapes, and the relationship between historic buildings and their wider setting.
## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
**Essential criteria**
You will have:
* A relevant academic or professional qualification in architectural history, buildings archaeology, archaeology or a related subject, or equivalent professional experience.
* Significant professional experience in historic building recording, buildings archaeology or a closely related area, including the investigation, analysis and interpretation of historic building fabric.
* Demonstrable experience of leading and designing historic building recording or comparable Built Heritage projects and producing high-quality technical and/or published outputs.
* Strong knowledge of British architectural history, together with specialist expertise in one or more relevant subject areas.
* Excellent research and analytical skills, including experience of using archival, documentary and physical evidence to develop robust interpretations of historic buildings and places.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical matters clearly to clients, colleagues, stakeholders and non-specialist audiences.
* Experience of providing technical leadership and quality assurance, including reviewing the work of others and managing or coordinating specialists and project teams.
* Experience of working collaboratively on multidisciplinary projects and engaging effectively with clients, Conservation Officers, statutory consultees and other heritage professionals.
* Experience of writing setting assessment, Built Heritage Statements, Conservation Area Appraisals and heritage impact assessment and contributing to Environmental Impact Assessments.
* A sound understanding of the UK legislative, planning policy and professional framework relevant to historic buildings and the wider historic environment.
* Experience of scoping and commercially managing projects, including preparation of fee proposals, budgets and programmes.
* Experience of mentoring, training or developing less experienced colleagues.
* A full, valid driving licence and willingness to travel to sites, archives and meetings and to work away from home for short periods where required.
For appointment at Principal level, MCIfA and/or an appropriate level of IHBC membership would normally be expected, or you should be able to demonstrate equivalent professional standing.
**Desirable criteria**
You may also have experience in one or more of the following:
* Major infrastructure or other large multidisciplinary heritage projects.
* Leading the analysis and publication of substantial programmes of Historic Building Recording.
* Agricultural buildings and landscapes.
* Military, wartime or aviation heritage.
* Railway heritage.
* Industrial buildings and landscapes.
* Entertainment, leisure or institutional architecture.
* Historic landscape analysis.
* Commissioning and managing specialist academic or professional contributors.
* Developing technical standards, methodologies, guidance or training.
* Public engagement and communicating buildings research to wider audiences.
* Professional or academic publication.
* Providing specialist advice at public inquiry, examination or comparable formal proceedings.
**About you**
We are looking for someone who combines strong technical knowledge with enthusiasm for understanding buildings and the people, activities and landscapes that shaped them.
You may come from a commercial archaeology, architectural history, Built Heritage consultancy, academic or conservation background. What matters most is that you can demonstrate a strong understanding of historic buildings, rigorous research and analytical skills and the ability to lead high-quality professional work.
You will be comfortable taking responsibility for technically complex projects while also working collaboratively with colleagues from different disciplines.
You will enjoy sharing your knowledge and developing others and will want to play an active role in shaping Headland’s Historic Building Recording capability.
## Benefits

## Job Description
# Domestic Abuse Complex Needs Specialist (Safe Accommodation)
**Location:** Manchester City **Salary:** 29,000 **Contract:** Permanent **Hours:** 40 hours per week **Working hours:** Flexible service rota, including core cover between 9am–10pm Monday to Friday, with agreed emergency/out-of-hours arrangements **DBS:** Enhanced DBS required
## About The Housing Network
At The Housing Network (THN), we believe everyone deserves more than a roof. We provide safe and stable accommodation alongside the support people need to rebuild their lives.
We are looking for a **Domestic Abuse Complex Needs Specialist** to join a new dispersed safe accommodation service supporting victims and survivors of domestic abuse and their children who may also be experiencing multiple and intersecting needs.
These may include homelessness, mental or physical ill health, substance use, disability, deprivation, social isolation and other barriers to safety, recovery and independence.
## About the role
As a Domestic Abuse Complex Needs Specialist, you will provide **person-centred, trauma-informed and strengths-based support** to victims and survivors living in safe accommodation.
You will build trusting relationships, assess risk and need, develop safety and support plans, and provide practical and emotional support to help residents move towards greater independence and sustainable accommodation.
The role combines **specialist domestic abuse support with housing management**, requiring you to work confidently with residents, colleagues and a wide range of external agencies.
### Key responsibilities
* Provide intensive one-to-one support, advocacy, practical assistance and group work.
* Build safe, respectful and trusting relationships with victims and survivors.
* Complete strengths-based assessments, DASH assessments, risk assessments and safety plans.
* Contribute to MARAC and other high-risk domestic abuse pathways.
* Support residents experiencing complex and intersecting needs, including mental ill health, substance use and homelessness.
* Safeguard adults and children, responding appropriately to serious or escalating concerns.
* Support residents with benefits, budgeting, debt, tenancy readiness and housing applications.
* Develop personalised move-on and resettlement plans to help residents access safe, sustainable accommodation.
* Work closely with domestic abuse services, Manchester City Council, police, health services, children's services, homelessness organisations and voluntary and community partners.
* Maintain accurate and timely case records and performance information.
* Promote resident choice, independence, resilience and long-term wellbeing.
* Support the safety and security of dispersed accommodation.
## About you
We are looking for someone with **demonstrable experience supporting victims and survivors of domestic abuse**, or closely related experience supporting people experiencing multiple disadvantage and complex needs.
You will have:
* Knowledge of domestic abuse, coercive control, trauma and its impact on individuals and families.
* Experience completing DASH assessments, safety plans and/or contributing to MARAC.
* Experience of safeguarding adults and children and managing risk.
* Experience of strengths-based, person-centred and trauma-informed support.
* Experience of accommodation-based support, housing management, benefits or move-on/resettlement.
* The ability to engage people who may have inconsistent engagement, using empathy, persistence and professional boundaries.
* Strong communication, advocacy, partnership-working and case-recording skills.
* A commitment to equality, diversity, inclusion, confidentiality and survivor choice.
* The ability to work flexibly across dispersed accommodation in Manchester.
### Qualifications and requirements
A **Level 2 qualification in Health & Social Care, Domestic Abuse, Housing or a related area** is desirable, or you must be willing to work towards an appropriate qualification.
Relevant training in domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice and risk assessment is desirable, with further development available.
An **Enhanced DBS** is required for this role.
You will need to be able to travel between dispersed accommodation and partner locations in Manchester. A full UK driving licence and company car and fuel card provided.
## Why join The Housing Network?
This is an opportunity to join a growing service at an important stage of its development and make a genuine difference to the lives of victims and survivors of domestic abuse.
You will play a key role in helping people move from crisis towards **safety, stability, independence and sustainable accommodation**, while working as part of a collaborative multi-agency network.
If you are passionate about supporting people affected by domestic abuse and complex needs, and want to use your skills to make a meaningful difference, we would love to hear from you.
**Apply now to join The Housing Network.**

If you are looking for an exciting new career opportunity, then join Shelter as a Housing Rights Worker and you could soon be making a real difference to people affected by the housing emergency.
**About the role**
Shelter Manchester are recruiting two Housing Rights Workers, as part of our @Home Service, to undertake preventative work with families at risk of homelessness, so that they can sustain a safe and secure home.
Your role will be to deliver high quality housing advice and advocacy in school settings to families at risk of becoming homeless and experiencing housing issues. You will plan and deliver holistic casework to families and support them to resolve their housing situation, as well as recording quantitative and qualitative data to evidence the impact of these interventions.
You will work within school and community settings to deliver rights awareness workshops to improve professional’s knowledge of local housing issues and raise awareness of housing rights
**About you**
You will have the ability to engage and work collaboratively with individuals, communities and a variety of stakeholders, including running group workshops and presentations. You have experience, knowledge of and/or proven ability in housing and homelessness advice and advocacy, with the ability to progress to specialist level knowledge. Essential to the role will be good time management, carrying out casework related interviews, maintaining detailed case records and offering advice and support to clients to inform their decisions.
**Benefits**
In return we offer a competitive salary as well as a wide range of benefits, including 30 days of annual leave (pro rata), enhanced family friendly policies, pension and interest free travel loans. Our employees also have access to a tenancy deposit loan, payroll giving, cycle to work scheme and an employee assistance programme.
**About the team**
You will be part of an existing multi-disciplinary team that offers housing and homelessness advice and support across Greater Manchester. It consists of a solicitor led legal team providing advice and representation, and an advice service providing advice, support and guided self-help to people with housing, debt or welfare benefit issues. There is also a committed and skilled team of volunteers that offer peer support, mentoring and more general volunteering adding significant value to our core service offer.
**About Shelter**
Home is a human right. It’s our foundation and where we thrive. Yet every day millions of people are being devastated by the housing emergency.
We exist to defend the right to a safe home. Because home is everything.

Join Hometree at the most exciting moment in our story. We're now going through the biggest step change in our history. By acquiring OVO Energy's Home Services division, including the trusted CORGI HomePlan and HomeHeat brands, we're becoming one of the UK's leading home services groups, with fresh investment to fuel our next phase of growth. **🏆 UK's third-largest home cover provider:** our latest acquisition makes us the third-largest provider of home cover in the UK.
🏆 **7 Acquisitions** - We've expanded our operations by acquiring 6 key companies across financing (Hometree Finance - formerly Bewarm), Home Cover (Your Repair) and energy services (Geowarmth, The Little Green Energy Company, IMS and GreenGen). 🏆 **500k Homes Covered** - We cover over 500 hundred thousand homes across the UK
🏆 **550+ Employees** - We have over 550 passionate employees transforming the industry across the Group, one home at a time
### The Role
You'll be the person responsible for health and safety across every business that installs for Hometree: heat pumps, solar, batteries and boilers, in homes all over the UK.
You'll set the standards, get out on site to see whether they're embedded, and put things right where they aren't. It's a broad brief with real autonomy, reporting straight into the Director of Operations, Installs and advising senior management through our Health and Safety Committee.
We're open on background. This is a step up for an experienced Health and Safety Advisor or Officer ready for their first manager role, and it's equally a good fit for an established Health and Safety Manager who wants the autonomy to shape a function rather than inherit one. **Responsibilities:**
* **Build and embed the installer health and safety framework**: policies, manuals, safe systems of work and emergency response plans, aligned to UK legislation, CDM 2015 and MCS scheme requirements, and built to support a Just Culture across the division
* **Lead the relationship with our external health and safety advisory provider**, drawing on their specialist expertise where you need it and making sure we get real value from it
* **Run the risk assessment programme** across both field activity (working at height, electrical isolation, refrigerant handling, manual handling, lone and remote working, driver safety) and premises (storage facilities, warehouses and installer offices, including fire risk assessment and racking inspection)
* **Set, communicate and audit the health and safety standards** our contractors and subcontractors work to, and verify competence at onboarding and in use
* **Coordinate investigations** into accidents, near misses and safety incidents: establish root cause, ensure RIDDOR compliance, produce toolbox talks and track corrective actions through to closure
* **Spend time on site building relationships**, coaching teams, constructively challenging unsafe behaviour and leading by example
* **Design and deliver training for employees, contractors and subcontractors**, and ensure sufficient trained resource across every installer business covering first aiders, fire wardens and local health and safety officers
* **Run the audit and inspection programme**, monitor compliance and maintain accurate documentation
* **Report performance, incidents, trends and recommendations to senior management** and the Health and Safety Committee, and advise on strategy, priorities and continuous improvement
**What we’re looking for:**
* NEBOSH National General Certificate (Level 3) or equivalent, with Tech IOSH membership or eligibility on appointment
* Experience coordinating health and safety across dispersed field teams and multiple sites, rather than a single fixed location
* Demonstrable experience authoring risk assessments for both field activity and premises, including storage facilities and offices
* Working knowledge of CDM 2015, or the appetite to get up to speed quickly on how duties apply where the client is a domestic householder
* Experience setting or auditing health and safety standards for subcontractors
* Excellent communication and stakeholder skills, with the credibility to influence senior leaders and engineers alike, and the confidence to lead without direct authority
* Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret incident and leading-indicator data, spot trends and turn them into action
* Full UK driving licence
***Extra Credit:***
* NEBOSH Diploma (Level 6), or working towards it
* Grad IOSH or CMIOSH
* NEBOSH Construction Certificate, SMSTS or SSSTS
* Fire risk assessor qualification (NEBOSH Fire Certificate or IFE Level 3)
* Experience in domestic renewables (air source heat pumps, solar PV, battery storage) or domestic heating
* ISO 45001 internal auditor, or experience of an accredited management system
* Experience bringing acquired businesses onto a single group health and safety standard

* **Initial Call:** Start with an introductory call with our Junior Talent Acquisition Specialist to discuss the role and your potential fit. (30 mins)
* **Hiring Manager Interview:** Engage in a detailed discussion about your past experiences with our Director of Operations, Installs (1 hr)
* **Task followed by Stakeholder Interview:** Task: Review Hometree Installations’ current health & safety framework and documentation and present improvements followed (45 mins) followed by stakeholder interview focused on values and cultural fit (45 mins - 90 mins total)
+ Presentation to Director of Operations, Installs, Director of Sales Operations, Installs and an Installer Managing Director
+ Followed by a stakeholder interview with the Director of Sales Operations, Installs and an Installer Managing Director
* **Final Interview:** For certain positions there may be a final interview with a member of senior management or our senior leadership team (30mins)
### **Perks of the job**
We have an ever expanding list of benefits that currently includes:
* 25 days holiday plus bank holidays and your birthday
* Hybrid working - with some nationwide travel required, particularly to Cornwall and Kent
* Free boiler & home emergency cover with Hometree plus 40% discount for friends & family
* Discounted gym membership across over 100 UK gyms (independent and chains) and free fitness, wellness and nutrition apps.
* £300 Home office allowance
* Support for your mental health and wellbeing via Oliva
* Menopause support from Stella, including friends & family access
* Cycle to work scheme
* Regular team socials including Summer and Winter parties.

## The HR Business Partner advises senior leaders across an international business, translating strategy into integrated people, organisation and workforce plans.
Looking for a challenge in one of the world’s largest airfreight logistics organisations?
At IAG Cargo we are in the business of moving things. From antibiotics to groundbreaking tech, gold bullion to avocados and everything in between. We move cargo that positively impacts society worldwide. Whatever people need, wherever they are. At IAG Cargo we open the skies and fly the world to bring people the things they really need. We are the logistics and cargo brand of International Airlines Group (Aer Lingus, British Airways, Iberia, Level and Vueling). Powered by five airlines, our reach is truly global – but it’s the impact we make that defines us. At IAG Cargo, we believe in keeping the world’s economies turning, and do everything with determined attitudes, curious minds, collaborative actions and heartfelt pride. Join us at our globally recognised logistics business, that is Trusted to Deliver.
#### **About the role**
The HR Business Partner advises senior leaders across an international business, translating strategy into integrated people, organisation and workforce plans. The role leads organisational design and change, talent and succession, performance and reward, employee relations and workforce insight across countries and business areas.
The role challenges and governs people decisions, leads complex international transformation and consultation, and works across HR, Reward, Talent, Legal and local specialist teams to deliver consistent, sustainable outcomes and a positive employee experience.
The HR Business Partner builds trusted relationships across cultures, countries and time zones, understands varied commercial, operational and regulatory contexts, and balances global consistency with local requirements. The role is solutions-focused, evidence-led and accountable for delivery.
#### **What you’ll do**
**Strategic business partnering and workforce planning**
* Translate business priorities into people, organisation and capability plans aligned with the IAG Cargo People strategy.
* Build trusted relationships and lead on complex or strategic people matters.
* Use external insight and HR best practice to improve decisions and organisational effectiveness.
**Organisational design, transformation and change governance**
* Lead and govern organisational design and people change from rationale and impact assessment through consultation and implementation.
* Ensure change follows agreed governance with input from Finance, Legal, Reward and other stakeholders.
* Advise leaders on change delivery, communications, consultation, risk and consistent people processes.
**Employee relations, employment law and wellbeing**
* Oversee complex employee relations matters, including grievances, discipline, capability, absence, settlements, redundancy and termination.
* Coach leaders to resolve people issues appropriately, strengthen capability and support wellbeing.
**Reward, pay and workforce cost governance**
* Partner with Reward, Finance and leaders on pay, bonus, job evaluation and remuneration decisions.
* Oversee annual pay and bonus cycles, including validation, exceptions, calibration, communications and sign-off.
**Talent, succession, performance and capability**
* Lead performance management and calibration, ensuring clear objectives, evidence-based assessments and consistent outcomes.
* Partner with Learning, Talent and Performance to build leadership, skills and capability.
**People analytics, reporting and organisational insight**
* Use people data to identify trends, risks and opportunities and recommend action.
* Support leadership reporting on workforce and people priorities.
* Test assumptions, identify root causes and inform evidence-based workforce decisions.
* Promote accurate, confidential and clearly owned workforce data.
**Leadership, facilitation and team development**
* Lead, coach and develop a high-performing HR Adviser team.
* Contribute to the wider HR agenda, improving consistency and delivering enterprise people priorities.
#### **It's all about you**
What you’ll bring to IAG Cargo:
* Strategic thinking, with the ability to connect business priorities, organisational design and people outcomes.
* A strong focus on delivery and close attention to detail.
* Strong influencing, facilitation and communication skills across senior, cross-functional and cross-cultural stakeholder groups.
* Strong analytical capability, including the ability to translate complex people data into clear executive insights and recommendations.
* Sound judgement and decision-making, with the ability to balance legal, employee, commercial and operational considerations.
* The ability to assess competing factors quickly and accurately while maintaining sight of the wider context.
* The ability to work effectively through ambiguity, manage competing priorities and remain resilient in sensitive or high-pressure situations.
* Strong leadership, coaching and people management capability.
* The resilience and tenacity to see work through to completion.
* A collaborative, inclusive, customer-focused and results-driven approach.
Skills and Experience:
* Strategic and operational experience as an HR Business Partner, ideally within a global organisation.
* Up-to-date knowledge of HR best practice and relevant employment legislation.
* A strong commitment to equity, diversity and inclusion, actively promoting an inclusive organisational culture.
* Experience working within a business partnering model to deliver positive outcomes with local leaders.
* Experience working constructively with trade unions.
* A proven record of delivering people-related change within a global organisation.
* Experience working in a group environment, supported by strong cross-cultural awareness.
#### We’ll treat you right
Wherever you work within IAG Cargo, you’ll play a part in helping us deliver what the world needs and join a diverse and inclusive business that’s making a difference.
As well as a competitive salary, bonus, we offer a range of benefits to support our colleagues, which include:
* A hybrid environment with 3 days a week in the office and two from home.
* From the day you join us, you’ll get access to brilliant staff travel benefits including unlimited basic and premium standby tickets on British Airways and group airlines. You’ll also receive up to 30 discounted ‘Hotline’ airfares per year for yourself, friends, and family.

* All our colleagues get access to LinkedIn learning and Rosetta Stone Language courses
* For health and wellbeing we offer a free onsite gym facility as well as access to the UNMIND app and a community of Mental Health First Aiders
* Access to discounts on Apple, Cinema tickets and loads of other goodies through Perks at work
